scope: Only the newly added segmentation_guard_get, segmentation_guard_unpack and native_segmentation_ready implementation; original segmentation implementation was separately reviewed.
conclusion: No blocking reference-lifetime, normal dependency-order or cleanup issue identified in this read-only review.
checked: Current/expected function values, class/state snapshots, method values, fields and iterator results are strongly owned before callbacks and allocations.
Exact tuple/list unpacking acquires references without invoking user iteration; generic unpacking consumes at most N+1 items and clears all acquired items on failure.
Class methods use ordinary attribute lookup; exact builtin metaclass fields use its stable type dictionary while custom metaclasses use attribute lookup and get.
Function checks precede class checks, method checks precede fields, and mismatches short-circuit in the reference order.
No readiness-result cache was introduced; subsequent ordinary class/helper mutations are observed.
limits: This receipt records source review, not an independent execution of the new 23-helper test suite.
It does not claim all arbitrary inputs or private guard-metadata globals rebound during an in-progress callback have the same observable semantics.
Native-design owner separately reported 22 segmentation tests passed; that test report is not relabeled as this agent's execution.
